title: IMF preparing El Nino assistance, concerned about AI bubble burst: chief to AFP
source_used: Arab News (AFP interview, El Nino) and Turkiye Today (AI remarks, same Singapore event)
key_facts: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told AFP in an interview in Singapore on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 that the IMF is preparing to support countries exposed to El Nino.
She said the IMF is concerned about food security and about inflation pressure from more expensive food.
Forecasters predict this year's El Nino will peak at an intensity never observed in the modern era (AFP text).
She warned of a 'risk of dual exogenous shocks': El Nino and higher energy prices from the US-Iran war.
She named Pacific island countries, Bangladesh and Laos as more vulnerable.
Turkiye Today reports she said AI could add up to half a percentage point of annual global growth, and that AI hardware and related products already make up more than 10% of world goods trade.
Turkiye Today reports she warned that a loss of confidence in AI could ripple through global markets and create financial stability risks.
Turkiye Today reports she said global public debt is on track to exceed 100% of GDP.
quote_evidence: We are very concerned about the El Nino that is hitting this year, Georgieva said in an interview in Singapore.
Equally, if there is loss of confidence and money runs away from AI, that can lead to financial stability risks.
why_it_matters_hint: The IMF is preparing help for vulnerable countries and warns that a loss of confidence in AI could hit financial stability.
notes: RFI original blocked (HTTP 403). The AFP interview is read on Arab News; Turkiye Today covers the same Singapore remarks on AI but does not credit AFP. The 'AI bubble burst' wording in the headline is not in either text; the summary uses Turkiye Today's wording.
